steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Salve, Cardinal Velliv, it's been a while.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Not 'cardinal' anymore. I'm just an ordinary clerk in the Shrine of Nurtury now.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Just 'Velliv', then? Anyway, it seems like your fingerprints are all over it.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: The security measures I saw on my way in from the streets. They could go toe-to-toe with the Pontifica Cohors.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: I have to earn my keep, after all.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Anyway, it looks like I guessed right.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: It was indeed you who came to review our security... even though this is a job usually reserved for Notarial Hall executors, or the gun-knights and Pontifica Cohors.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I'm still investigating the bombing that happened a couple of days ago. I'm not exactly an outsider.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: I wasn't instructed to take the bomb investigation into account when planning security. Besides, your investigation hasn't exactly turned up anything concrete, has it?

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Unless you mean to tell me you came because it was Andoain who was attacked?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Are you going to chide me that I should be thinking of the whole Holy City as a cardinal of the Seventh Tribunal, and not about my personal relationships?

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: We know just what kind of person you are.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Sharp, astute, decisive, all traits that served you well at the consistory...

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: But we also know when these virtues of yours are most prominently displayed.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: I remember the reasons why you joined the Pontifica Cohors commandos, Cardinal Lemuen. I read that report.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Hah. Do you really? I've forgotten.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: You didn't really have any interest in the commandos. You just went to see Fiammetta, didn't you?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: And Andoain.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Really? That I didn't know. I thought you met after you joined the commandos.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: We met before that.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: It seemed like he had come from a far away place, walking on foot. His clothes were tattered, and he himself was just as ragged.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: He sat on a bench in front of the chapel, still and unmoving, looking more like a statue than the actual statues of the saints on the roadside.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: That was the first time Mostima and I saw him.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: We met Fiammetta at the midnight movies. We hit it off quickly.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Andoain had trouble fitting in, having grown up outside the Holy City. Fiammetta, stubborn girl that she is, was in another one of those fights with her grandpa... Mostima and I wanted to see them.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: They didn't know each other beforehand, and the other Sanktas probably didn't intend to isolate them, but either way, the end result was—

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: The two of them were the only ones left behind in the rubber-bullet roulette that was the commandos' initiation.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: And so you beat up everyone else on the scene...

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: You and Mostima filled out your applications right there, becoming the last four-man squad at that initiation.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: You ended up being the most active and most coordinated squad on the force, until the incident...

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: There is a lot I admire about you, Lemuen, but I must remind you... as a cardinal, the Holy City must be your first, foremost, and only concern.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: To me, the Holy City begins with a long list of familiar names.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: So much for reminiscing.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: The Seventh Tribunal knows our duty. If you really think of yourself as an ordinary clerk, then maybe I should pay a visit to the Matriarch personally.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: She's right up ahead, isn't she?
Lemuen spots the one she came to see.
The golden-haired Sankta stands under a porch. She is praying, anxious; her breathing is rapid, and she trembles visibly...
Lemuen can feel herself overwhelmed by her counterpart's raging emotions.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Matriarch?

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: I overheard your conversation with Velliv, Cardinal Lemuen... pardon my inability to converse calmly at this time.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: What's in there?

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: A Sarkaz mother.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: She spent much time in the wilderness, and declined food for two days after she arrived... she is not in good shape. Our Nurturers are doing their best.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: She suffers from fear and anxiety. She does not want to give in to the pain, and continues her struggle to stay awake...

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: She is praying, awake, praying that her child will be born safely.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: All I can do is empathize and pray with her.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: You can empathize with a Sarkaz?

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Yes, Cardinal.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: As you worry for my outpouring of emotion. It is as clear as the innate empathy between you and I.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: 'Empathy'...

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: A blessing that the Lord has bestowed upon me, perhaps, in place of my sight... or perhaps simply because this place was built by Laterano to welcome new life.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Here our faith is strengthened and expanded. Here, there are no barriers, no limits.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Putting it in that light, it is our own people who need this place the most.
Sunlight shines through the stained glass, illuminating the empty and solemn hall.
The massive statue stands with its palms together, looking down on the two tiny Sanktas beneath it.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: It's certainly a special place.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I've seen plenty of statues in all sorts of poses, holding a gun and ready to shoot. But it's the first time I've seen one like this, and it takes some getting used to.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Compared to the so-called 'Lateran statues' that line the hills of Bolívar or the shores of Iberia, the statues seen in Laterano are the more incomprehensible, Cardinal.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Paradise has shaped our faith, so peculiar that it has become somewhat distorted.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: The souls of the living praying for survival, as they traverse Catastrophe and suffering... such is the most basic face of faith.

steps.name: Nurturer
steps.text: M-Matriarch. Blessings to you.

steps.name: Nurturer
steps.text: The mother's condition has stabilized. We have given her medicine and nutrition. She is sleeping now.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: That is comforting to hear.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: She is expecting soon. Please keep a close eye on her, and do not let yourselves grow complacent.

steps.name: Nurturer
steps.text: Yes, Matriarch.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Praise be to the Lord.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I can feel the relief and joy coming from the bottom of your heart.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Thank you for your companionship, Cardinal. I hope empathy did not cause my anxiety to affect you.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I'm not so weak. Besides, your words were inspiring, to an extent.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: You mentioned that you only came here later?

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Long had I wandered the wilderness, my companions withered in the mud...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: In order to find Laterano?

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: No, at the time I never imagined that there would be such a city upon this land.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: But our shared vision finally helped me locate it.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Our encounter here and now was written in fate.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: It is a blessing to be able to serve Laterano and my kindred, after all this time, frail as I may be.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I have a friend who works here. He also came from afar...

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: In Laterano today and Laterano tomorrow, everyone must and will find their own place and play their own roles... only then can we hope to fend off calamity.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: It seems we've gotten sidetracked.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: If there has been an attack on the Nurturers, the Seventh Tribunal is happy to work with the Shrine of Nurtury in implementing security measures, to ensure that the Nativity goes off without a hitch.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: I understand your worry for your friend, and your curiosity about this shrine.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: As I said, though, we must all find our own place and play our own roles.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: And there I was, thinking our chat was going nicely.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Looks like I've been summarily rejected, haven't I?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: ...I'm sorry for your loss.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: I should have brought a few wheat stalks, if I only knew this had happened.

steps.name: Kuranta
steps.text: Wheat stalks?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: For funerals at the Landen Monastery, we weave a laurel out of wheat stalks and place it upon the departed's coffin.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: That way, the soul of the departed will be comforted by the scent of bread and beer on the other side.

steps.name: Kuranta
steps.text: Thank you, kind sister.

steps.name: Kuranta
steps.text: My brother and I were exiled by the General Chamber of Commerce because we were afflicted with Oripathy, and did not have the skill to participate in knightsports.

steps.name: Kuranta
steps.text: We came all this way to Laterano, only for his condition to worsen and take his life...

steps.name: Kuranta
steps.text: But the Curia helped bury him, allowing him to die with dignity... there was even a passing Sankta who played a requiem for him.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: I see...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Was that Sankta a female with long, straight black hair, playing a cello with an unusual shape?

steps.name: Kuranta
steps.text: Er, yes.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: She played for you?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Were you subject to any hallucinations, or any psychological discomfort?

steps.name: Kuranta
steps.text: What do mean by discomfort? I know it made me cry. It was my brother, after all...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Senior Executor, I thought we agreed that I would do the questioning...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Other executors from Notarial Hall will soon be here to take these refugees to Pagus Ambrosius. We do not have much time.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: They are not suspected of any crime. I did not find complex interrogation techniques to be necessary.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: I visited Lungmen and Victoria when I was promoting Landen Monastery, and I saw many people like them.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: They were forced to leave home due to unfortunate circumstances. Their previous dealings with the police have made them...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Executors are more or less police, right?

steps.name: Kuranta
steps.text: Uh, there's no need. You guys just took in outsiders with Oripathy like us, even though I heard you used to kick your own Infected out.

steps.name: Kuranta
steps.text: So, right now, I don't have anything against the Lateran government. Besides, this gentleman here looks like a decent fellow...

steps.name: Kuranta
steps.text: Is there something wrong with the black-haired Sankta you were asking about?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Without permission, she left the monastery where she was under observation. We have tracked her here.

steps.name: Kuranta
steps.text: Sh-She's a prisoner? I thought she was an official from your, what's that, Sixth Tribunal?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Why did you think that?

steps.name: Kuranta
steps.text: She asked us about the abbey after the funeral, whether there was any equipment in disrepair, any safety hazards, any supplies we were short on.

steps.name: Kuranta
steps.text: She made it a point to ask if anyone who recently entered Laterano had disappeared, especially any pregnant women...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: (Doesn't sound like Arturia just happened to pass by...)

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: How did it go?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: You know the answer.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: The Matriarch's response was just like yours—'don't poke your head into other people's business.'

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Hehe.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: I know you have good intentions, Lemuen, but you're also showing that you don't trust me.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: I beg your understanding.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: The Shrine of Nurtury, this great structure that casts a shadow over Laterano, which no one's quite sure when it came to be...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: You, Reverend Patrizion and the Matriarch promise that this will be the birthplace of the future. Even the suspect behind the bombings seems interested in it.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: How can the Seventh Tribunal, responsible for intelligence and national security, ignore something so prominent?

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Of course, I understand.

steps.name: Guiding Nurturer
steps.text: Excuse me.
The Nurturer leads a group past. Their footsteps echo through the empty hall.
The people in the procession come from many different races. None of them speak, but all glance up and down at this unfamiliar space.
Lemuen steps aside to let them pass.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: What is it, Cardinal Lemuen?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Nothing.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: What I mean is, curiosity killed the Feline. I guess I should expect a complaint from my predecessor if I continue to insist.
